title: CLO6.2 New Features Live Broadcast Replay
description: CLO6.2 New Features Live Replay is Here~~~~~ Unlimited new CLO features waiting for you to discover!

The main functions are BGN's rain costume, folding 3D costume, riding horse, replacement version, and using Colossus assets in Clo.  

First, let's take a look at the first main function: BGN's rain costume.  
BGN's rain costume.

We can see that this is the final presentation effect.  
You can see that.

You can also click the last fill tool in the 2D window 2D toolbar.

Next, let's make a selection and copy of the fill tool.

Select the fill tool.  
Go to the property editor here.

Then, according to the ratio of press and hold,  
there are a total of four options here.  
Click on it.  
You can see the four options.  
Choose one of them.  
Click on it.  

Next is the weight input.  
Enter the weight of the fill tool as required.  
Here you have to pay attention:  
When selecting multiple sheets to set the total weight of the fill tool,  
the fill tool weight of each sheet is assigned according to the ratio of the area.  

Next, set the width of the air vent.  
Enter the width of the air vent.  
Here you must note:  
If the air vent line is regular and equidistant,  
you can enter the number directly.  
If it is irregular, you need to enter the maximum width of the air vent line.  
Because the fill tool size is calculated according to the weight of the fill tool and the width of the air vent.

Next, set the fill tool for other sheets.

Enter the weight and the width of the air vent.

Set the weight of each sheet according to the agreement class requirements.  

After input is complete, set the horizontal line of the sheet according to the actual effect.

After enlarging, click the fill tool.  
First, turn off the previously set lock on the sheet external line.  
Go to the sleeve here.  
Click the horizontal line.  
At this time, the horizontal line changes from purple to gray.  
Simulate.  

Oh, maybe some students feel that the sound is a little small, right?  
Then I will increase the volume a bit.  
Is the sound louder now?  
Is the sound louder now?  
Okay, I will continue to talk.  
Okay, I will continue to talk.  
I will continue to talk.  

At this time, we can see that the horizontal line here changed from purple to gray.  
Then simulate.  
Pay attention to the horizontal line in the 3D window here.  
Is the original horizontal mark gone?  
That means the inside and outside layers of this place have been eliminated.  

How to restore its horizontal line?  
Still use the fill tool.  
Click the horizontal line here on the sleeve.  
Let it change from gray to purple.

Simulate again.  

At this time, the inside and outside layers of this place have become normal.  
Simulate until stable.  
You can see this is the final effect.  

Next, select the outer layer of the panel frame.  
Go to the parameter editor.  
Look at the last function.  
This function is the real horizontal line.  
If you want your horizontal line to show a V-shaped effect,

Pay attention to the effect in the 3D window.  
After enabling it, you can see the change in the 3D window.  
Simulate and add details.  
Its final presentation effect is the same as my file.  
Let's take a look.  
This is the final effect.  
Rotate it.  
Look at different angles.  
Zoom in.

Next, let's look at a comparison.  
The same fill object, the same width of the horizontal line,

chunks.title: CLO6.2 New Features Live Broadcast Replay
chunks.content: ## Overview of CLO 6.2 New Features This document details the new features introduced in CLO version 6.2, focusing on BGN rain costume creation, 3D clothing folding, horse simulation, panel replacement, cloud asset usage, mode updates (print/release and check code), material functions, and various function optimizations including virtual model handling, 2D improvements, and file management. Technical procedures, tool descriptions, parameter settings, and examples are provided to facilitate effective use of the software. --- ## 1. BGN Rain Costume Creation and Fill Tool Settings This section covers the creation of BGN rain costumes using fill and weight settings, including detailed instructions on using the fill tool to simulate realistic raincoat effects. - **BGN Rain Costume Function**: Allows creation of rain costumes by setting fill tool parameters such as fill type, weight, and air vent width. - **Fill Tool Location**: Accessible via the 2D panel toolbar or main menu. - **Copy and Fill Layers**: Select fill tools using cross or Shift selection, then copy layers by clicking on a blank area. - **Fill Tool Settings**: - **Category**: Four main fill tool categories based on press-and-hold ratios. - **Weight Input**: Total weight distributed proportionally by sheet area. - **Air Vent Width**: Enter numerical values; if irregular, input maximum width to calculate fill tool size. - **Setting Horizontal Lines**: - Lock external sheet outline. - Select all horizontal lines and set ratio value (e.g., 97) in the data editor. - **Simulation**: - Run simulation after input to generate automatic fill. - Adjust model posture and sleeve horizontal lines to demonstrate effect. - Horizontal line color changes indicate inside/outside layer visibility. - Real horizontal line effect can be toggled in parameter editor for V-shaped appearance. - **Effect Comparisons**: - Weight variations (e.g., 100g vs. 60g goose feather) impact fill appearance. - Real vs. virtual horizontal lines alter realism of fill effect. --- ## 2.
